title: Λύχνος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 232 (= Perry 349). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Μεθύων λύχνος ἐλαίῳ καὶ φέγγων ἐκαυχᾶτο ὡς ὑπὲρ ἥλιον πλέον λάμπει.
sentences.tr: Methyōn lychnos elaiōi kai phengōn ekauchato hōs hyper hēlion pleon lampei.
sentences.l: A lamp, drunk with oil and giving light, was boasting that it shines more than the sun.
sentences.i: A lamp, drunk with oil and shining out, boasted that it shone brighter than the sun.
sentences.n: μεθύω, 'to be drunk', takes the dative of what one is drunk on; a lamp filled to the brim is drunk with its oil. After ὡς the verb keeps the tense it would have had in the lamp's own words — present λάμπει, 'I shine' — where English shifts back to 'shone'.

sentences.t: Ἀνέμου δὲ πνοῆς συρισάσης, εὐθὺς ἐσβέσθη.
sentences.tr: Anemou de pnoēs syrisasēs, euthys esbesthē.
sentences.l: But a breath of wind having whistled, at once it was put out.
sentences.i: But a gust of wind whistled by, and it was snuffed out at once.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute, and a very short one: the whole reversal takes four words. συρίζω is the verb for the piping of a shepherd's reed, so the wind does not roar here, it whistles.

sentences.t: Ἐκ δευτέρου δὲ ἅπτων τις εἶπεν αὐτῷ· « Φαῖνε, λύχνε, καὶ σίγα· τῶν ἀστέρων τὸ φέγγος οὔποτε ἐκλείπει. »
sentences.tr: Ek deuterou de haptōn tis eipen autōi· « Phaine, lychne, kai siga· tōn asterōn to phengos oupote ekleipei. »
sentences.l: And someone, kindling it for a second time, said to it: « Shine, lamp, and be silent; the light of the stars never gives out. »
sentences.n: ἐκλείπω is the ordinary word for a light failing, and the noun from it, ἔκλειψις, is our 'eclipse'. The lamp had measured itself against the sun; the answer sets the stars against it instead, because their light is the light that does not fail.

sentences.t: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ τινα ἐν ταῖς δόξαις καὶ τοῖς λαμπροῖς τοῦ βίου τυφοῦσθαι· ὅσα γὰρ ἂν κτήσηταί τις, ξένα τυγχάνει.
sentences.tr: Hoti ou dei tina en tais doxais kai tois lamprois tou biou typhousthai· hosa gar an ktēsētai tis, xena tynchanei.
sentences.l: That one must not be puffed up at the glories and the splendours of life; for whatever a man acquires proves to be another's.
sentences.i: The story shows that one must not be puffed up at the glories and splendours of life; for whatever a man acquires proves to belong to someone else.
sentences.n: A bare Ὅτι moral: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek and is supplied in the idiomatic line. τυφόομαι is to be fuddled with conceit — the root τῦφος is smoke, and the image suits a lamp. ξένα is the predicate of τυγχάνει, 'turns out foreign', i.e. never really one's own.
